queue.claim: Whole-face asymmetry, as RMSD against the registered mirror, is about 0.8 mm in normal people: 0.80 ± 0.24 mm in healthy 3dMD volunteers, attributed to PMC4614853 and possibly from Taylor et al. 2014, J Craniofac Surg; and 0.8 ± 0.2 mm in 191 subjects (Linden et al. 2018). This calibrates the engine's asymmetry prior and the RMSD sanity bounds (0.3–1.5 mm).

queue.claim: Right–left differences at 9 bilateral soft-tissue landmark pairs were 0.6–4.6 mm in 48 adults with normal occlusion (CBCT), larger at lower and lateral landmarks. This is the basis for the per-region sigma_sym priors (0.7–4 mm per axis).

queue.claim: Perception thresholds: eyelid position at rest is about 2 mm (2017 review). Asymmetry under about 3–4 mm or 3–4° of canting is generally not recognised (attributed to PMC11595402, 'Limits in the Perception of Facial Symmetry', 2024; attribution unconfirmed).
